name: cavemio-filter-bar
title: Filter bar
description: The bar above a list, done like Linear’s: one panel from property to value, chips you change in place, and a sentence that becomes filters.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The panel's field is a combobox over a listbox: ↑ and ↓ move the highlight, Enter chooses, → opens a property, ← or Backspace in an empty field goes back, Escape goes back and then closes. Focus stays in the field the whole time and returns to whatever opened the panel.
- Each chip is a group named by its whole sentence ("Status is any of Todo, In progress"). Its operator and value are buttons with their own names, and × removes it. Adds, changes and removals are announced in a status region outside the bar.
- Chips glide only when one arrives or leaves: their places are taken at the click, the new layout is read once, and each one moves by a transform. Nothing runs between changes, and the panel animates its own box once per open and close.
- On narrow containers the chips stay on one line and scroll sideways; the panel fits the container's width. Inputs use 16px text on touch screens so phones don't zoom.
- Reduced motion opens, steps and adds in place; ticks, labels and the count still change.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: fields
props.description: – · { id, label, type, icon?, options?, unit?, get? }. type is "option" (pick values), "text" (contains), "number" (at least, at most, exactly) or "date" (within or older than a number of days).

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: – · The filters: { id, field, op, values } for options, { …, text } for text, { …, number } for numbers, { …, days } for dates.

props.name: count / total
props.description: – · How many rows match, and how many there are: "37 of 128 issues" rolls beside the bar. Leave count out when the list shows its own.

props.name: noun
props.description: ["result", "results"] · What a row is called, for the count.

props.name: parse
props.description: – · Turns a sentence into filters. Adds "Filter by “…”" to the panel for searches of three letters or more. Throw, or return none, to say it couldn't.

props.name: hotkey
props.description: "f" · Opens the panel from anywhere on the page while nothing is being typed. null turns it off.

props.name: locales
props.description: – · For numbers in chips and the count.

props.name: matchFilters(rows, filters, fields)
props.description: – · Keeps the rows every filter allows, reading each field with get (or row[id]). Arrays match an option filter if any value does.

useCases.title: Issue trackers and project tools
useCases.description: Filter by status, priority and assignee, like Linear.

useCases.title: CRM and customer lists

useCases.title: Admin tables and logs
useCases.description: Narrow a long table with the same chips on every screen.

useCases.title: Search by sentence

features.title: One panel, property to value
features.description: Filter opens a panel under the button. Pick a property and its values slide in, then the chip lands in the bar.

features.title: Search finds both at once
features.description: Typing “hig” offers Priority › High straight away. Text, number and date properties turn what you type into choices.

features.title: Chips you change in place
features.description: Click “is” and it becomes “is not”. Click the value and the panel reopens from the chip with its values ticked.

features.title: Describe it in a sentence
features.description: Give it parse() and the panel offers “Filter by …”. Your model returns chips, which rise into the bar.

features.title: Filters are plain data
features.description: They go straight into a query string, and matchFilters() applies them to rows you already have.

features.title: Keyboard first
features.description: Press F anywhere to open the panel, move with the arrow keys, and every chip is named by its whole sentence for screen readers.

states.title: open
states.description: Filter (or F anywhere on the page while nothing is being typed) grows the panel out from under the button: width, height and radius ease from the button's size in 300ms while the list fades in after 60ms. It never covers the bar, and it narrows and shifts to fit the container.

states.title: step
states.description: Choosing a property slides its values in 16px from the right (240ms) while the properties slide out left, and the panel's height eases to the new list. Back, Backspace or ← in an empty field, or Escape, slides back.

states.title: search
states.description: The field searches properties and every option's values together; a value match reads Priority › High and adds its filter in one go. Text, number and date properties turn what you type into choices: Contains “north”, At least 20 seats, Last 12 days.

states.title: add
states.description: The new chip rises 6px into the bar out of a blur (320ms) while Filter and Clear glide aside and the panel folds back. A value for a property already in the bar with the same operator joins that chip instead of making another.

states.title: flip
states.description: Clicking the operator cycles it (is ↔ is not, contains ↔ doesn't contain, at least → at most → is exactly, within ↔ older than) through TextMorph; the chip's width eases and its neighbours follow.

states.title: edit
states.description: Clicking a value opens the panel from that chip with its values ticked: ticks draw themselves, "Todo" morphs to "Todo, In progress" and "is" to "is any of", and "2 selected" rolls. A chip with nothing ticked goes when the panel closes.

states.title: describe
states.description: With parse, any search of three letters or more ends with Filter by “…”. While it runs the row says so beside a spinner; the chips it returns rise in one after another, 70ms apart. If it throws or finds nothing, the row shakes and says it couldn't, and your words stay to edit.

states.title: remove
states.description: A removed chip fades where it stood (its own element, so nothing waits for it) while the rest glide into the gap; Clear does it for all of them.
